raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County, so I will keep to the system I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize on most of my land. That fits our local weather, my age, my experience, and the kind of work I know how to manage without taking on too much risk. Wheat gives me a steady main crop, and maize after wheat makes full use of the land through the year. If I have a small piece of lighter land, I will put some peanuts on it in spring because they sell well and spread my risk a little, but I will not make peanuts my main crop because wheat-maize is what I know best and what I can manage most reliably. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters, put most fertilizer into wheat and maize because they respond well, irrigate when the crop is most sensitive, and keep pesticide use limited to when I think pest or disease pressure is worth the cost. I will plough or rotary till where I need a clean seedbed, then manage the crops in a simple, practical way focused on stable yield rather than chasing the highest possible output.
